rationale: All three applicable lenses ran; acceptance was skipped because this is a genuine no-spec round, so confidence is low. The non-v2 schema compatibility candidate remains blocking at major with production reachability unconfirmed: LangChain accepts v1 schemas, but no in-repository v1 tool schema was located, and ordinary v1 validation errors bypass the unchanged v2 exception handler rather than reaching the formatter. There are 0 deferred and 1 dismissed findings (annotation-only style without an explicitly blocking guide rule); tests and gates were not rerun because Stage 6 owns executable proof, and the fix pack was intentionally not written under the dispatch's verdict/brief/deferred-only write authorization.

standards_review.notes: The single commit subject in diff_base..HEAD matches the EPMCDME-####: Description format documented in .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md.

Reviewed the three Git-tracked changed files against .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md and the repository Ruff configuration without running gates. Production changes retain typed validation methods and remain within the service's existing responsibility; existing Apache headers are preserved. Newly added public regression functions and the model validator lack explicit parameter or return annotations, and ValidationInput.observed uses an unparameterized dict inside ClassVar[list[dict]], contrary to the guide's Types And Imports requirements.

Reviewed the changed validation and regression-test code against .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md. Argument validation now passes the received mapping directly to the existing schema instead of injecting omitted values as None; malformed values still enter the existing rejection path. Signature construction reads model field annotations rather than input values. No changed authentication logic, credential configuration, sensitive logging, or concrete security issue was found. Existing logging and schema coercion behavior are unchanged. Tests, builds, formatters, and linters were not run.

findings.title: Error formatting assumes v2 schema metadata
findings.problem: The caught validation-error/TypeError path now accesses tool.args_schema.model_fields unconditionally instead of the previous annotation interface. The installed LangChain BaseTool explicitly accepts Pydantic v1 schema classes, which do not expose model_fields. If such a schema raises a TypeError that escapes its constructor, the formatter raises AttributeError instead of the intended ValueError. Ordinary Pydantic v1 ValidationError is not caught by the unchanged v2 ValidationError handler and therefore does not demonstrate this new failure.
findings.impact: A tool using an accepted non-v2 schema could have a caught TypeError masked by AttributeError during direct-credential, system-integration, or file-analysis invocation. Production reachability was unconfirmed: no in-repository v1 tool schema was located, and the plugin/toolkit entry points inspected do not establish a v2-only schema boundary. Severity is capped at major rather than claiming a confirmed runtime regression.
findings.recommendation: Preserve safe signature formatting for accepted model schemas without model_fields, using compatible field metadata or a safe annotation fallback; alternatively establish and enforce a v2-only boundary before this validator. Confirm the applicable schema contract rather than broadening execution normalization or changing dependencies.
